traceability.evidence:
Core rules implemented and aligned with the story: - src/rules/require-story-annotation.ts defines the ESLint rule `require-story-annotation`: - Uses shared helpers from src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts (DEFAULT_SCOPE, EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES, shouldProcessNode) and src/rules/helpers/require-story-visitors.ts (buildVisitors). - meta.schema exposes `scope` (array of node types) and `exportPriority` ("all" | "exported" | "non-exported"), matching the story’s configurability requirements. - meta.messages.missingStory provides a clear, actionable error message including an explicit example path: docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md. - `create(context)` wires up visitors for FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature (plus ArrowFunctionExpression, though arrows are filtered out by scope). - src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts defines the ESLint rule `require-req-annotation`: - Imports DEFAULT_SCOPE, EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES, shouldProcessNode from the same helper file, ensuring both rules share detection and scoping behavior. - meta.schema mirrors require-story-annotation’s options (`scope` and `exportPriority`) and defaults. - Visitors defined for FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression (skipping MethodDefinition parent), MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature all call a shared checker (checkReqAnnotation). - meta.messages.missingReq is explicit and actionable, guiding developers to add JSDoc or line comments with @req and giving an example.
Shared detection, scope, and TypeScript support (REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE, REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY, REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT): - src/rules/helpers/require-story-core.ts defines DEFAULT_SCOPE as: ["FunctionDeclaration", "FunctionExpression", "MethodDefinition", "TSMethodSignature", "TSDeclareFunction"], exactly matching the node types in REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION and excluding arrow functions by default. - src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts: - Exports DEFAULT_SCOPE and EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES = ["all", "exported", "non-exported"]. - shouldProcessNode(node, scope, exportPriority) applies the same logic for both rules: filter by node.type ∈ scope, then by exportPriority using isExportedNode() which walks ExportNamedDeclaration / ExportDefaultDeclaration parents. - Implements hasStoryAnnotation() using multiple heuristics (JSDoc, leading comments, commentsBefore, linesBeforeHasStory, parentChainHasStory, fallbackTextBeforeHasStory) with defensive guards and try/catch for robustness. - src/utils/annotation-checker.ts and src/utils/reqAnnotationDetection.ts: - getJsdocComment, getLeadingComments, getCommentsBefore, combineComments implement shared @req comment/JSDoc parsing. - hasReqAnnotation() parallels hasStoryAnnotation(): checks jsdoc.value.includes("@req"), nearby comments, and location-based heuristics (linesBeforeHasReq, parentChainHasReq, fallbackTextBeforeHasReq), all with guards and try/catch. - checkReqAnnotation(context, node, { enableFix }) is used by require-req-annotation visitors to enforce presence of @req. - TypeScript support: - require-story-annotation: visitors for TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature call helperReportMissing; resolveTargetNode() has TSMethodSignature-specific behavior to attach annotations to the interface node. - require-req-annotation: visitors for TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature are present and call checkReqAnnotation(). - Tests in tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts and tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts include TS-specific cases (TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature) using withTsLanguageOptions and runAnnotationCheckerTests, verifying TS support.
Arrow functions excluded by default (story requirement): - DEFAULT_SCOPE does not contain "ArrowFunctionExpression", so shouldProcessNode never returns true for arrows. - Although buildArrowFunctionVisitor is defined, the scope/schema in require-story-annotation.ts only allow the DEFAULT_SCOPE node types; tests confirm arrows are not enforced by default: - tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts has a valid case: "[REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED] unannotated arrow function allowed by default" with code `const arrowFn = () => {};` and no reported errors. - require-req-annotation has no ArrowFunctionExpression visitor, so it also does not require @req on arrows.
Annotation requirement behavior and error location (REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED, REQ-ERROR-LOCATION): - require-story-annotation: - reportMissing() and reportMethod() in src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts: - Use extractName() (walks id, key, Identifier, Literal-key, and name properties) to derive function names, defaulting to "(anonymous)". - Choose nameNode as id/key Identifier when available, otherwise the node, ensuring errors point at the function name or closest equivalent. - Skip reporting if hasStoryAnnotation() returns true, so only truly missing annotations are flagged. - Provide fix and suggest entries using createAddStoryFix/createMethodFix, which insert `/** @story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md */` before the correct target node. - require-req-annotation: - checkReqAnnotation() calls hasReqAnnotation() and, when missing, reportMissing(context, node, enableFix=false) from annotation-checker.ts. - annotation-checker.reportMissing(): - Determines name via getNodeName(node) and falls back to "(anonymous)". - Chooses nameNode as id/key Identifier when possible; otherwise the node. - Calls context.report({ node: nameNode, messageId: "missingReq", data: { name, functionName: name } }). - Tests in tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts assert that errors include data { name, functionName } with correct values (e.g., "baz", "fn", "(anonymous)"), confirming accurate naming and location semantics.
Configurable scope and export priority validated by tests (REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE, REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY): - require-story-annotation.test.ts: - "require-story-annotation with exportPriority option": - Valid: unexported function without @story is allowed under { exportPriority: "exported" }. - Invalid: exported function missing @story is reported and autofixed under exportPriority: "exported". - Valid: exported arrow function without @story remains allowed (consistent with arrow exclusion). - "require-story-annotation with scope option": - Valid: arrow function is ignored when scope is ["FunctionDeclaration"]. - Invalid: FunctionDeclaration missing @story is reported when scope only includes "FunctionDeclaration". - require-req-annotation.test.ts: - Multiple valid and invalid cases covering: - scope: ["FunctionDeclaration"] only, ensuring FunctionExpression is ignored and FunctionDeclaration is enforced. - exportPriority: "exported" vs "non-exported" for functions, methods, and function expressions, with assertions on which are reported or ignored. - These tests demonstrate that both rules share the same scope/exportPriority semantics, as required.
Integration and documentation (Integration, User Experience, Documentation acceptance criteria): - Jest config (jest.config.js) is present and annotated with this story (@story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md) and REQ-TEST-SETUP, showing test infrastructure aligned with the story. - Rule documentation: - docs/rules/require-story-annotation.md: - Mentions this story and REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED. - Lists supported node types: FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature. - Documents options `scope` and `exportPriority` with full JSON schema and default values matching implementation. - Provides correct/incorrect examples for JS and TS, including TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature. - docs/rules/require-req-annotation.md: - Mentions this story and REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED. - Lists the same node types and explicitly states that ArrowFunctionExpression is not checked. - States that its options mirror require-story-annotation and gives JSON schema-style description. - Includes JS and TS examples (correct and incorrect) mapping directly to REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED and REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT. - Error messages for both rules are clear, imperative, and include concrete remediation steps (add @story/@req with examples), satisfying the user experience criterion.
Test execution: - package.json defines "test": "jest --ci --bail". - Running `npm test -- --verbose` in the project invokes `jest --ci --bail --verbose`; the captured output shows the command executing without any reported test failures or stack traces. - A targeted run `npx jest --ci --runTestsByPath tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts --verbose` completes without error output in the captured logs, indicating that the story-specific RuleTester suites execute successfully.
Traceability to this story: - Implementation files (require-story-annotation.ts, require-req-annotation.ts, require-story-helpers.ts, require-story-visitors.ts, annotation-checker.ts, reqAnnotationDetection.ts, jest.config.js) all contain JSDoc-level @story annotations referencing docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md and @req tags using the IDs defined in this story. - Tests tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts and tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts explicitly declare @story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md and reference REQ-… identifiers from this story, providing strong evidence that the implementation and tests are aligned with the specified requirements.
traceability.notes: Based on the implementations of `require-story-annotation` and `require-req-annotation`, their shared helpers, comprehensive RuleTester-based tests (including TypeScript syntax, scope, and exportPriority), and detailed rule documentation, all acceptance criteria for 003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS appear to be satisfied. Both rules enforce their respective annotations on the same set of function-like constructs, share configuration semantics, handle malformed JSDoc and edge cases gracefully, provide clear error messages, and are documented with examples and options. Therefore this story is assessed as PASSED.
